need: A new check on an existing repository fails on work written before it. The project either postponed the check until the old work was cleaned, which did not happen, or exempted old files, which let them keep growing the same fault.
evidence: One project introduced five checks this way in one week: a linter, a type checker, suppressions without a reason, assertions that restate source text and real-time waits in tests. Each records a count per file that may fall and never rise, with a new file starting at zero, and each refusal names the lines and the fix. The linter started at 1,203 findings in 480 files and the type checker at 60 in 9, so neither could have been turned on as a plain pass or fail; the real-time count started at 585 in 187 test files. Introducing the suppression count removed 240 unused suppressions, and reading the restated assertions removed 181 from one family.
limits: Observed in one project over about a week, so the evidence shows the checks could be turned on at once and that some counts fell, not a long-term trend. This is guidance: the kit adds no counting tool, because what is counted is the project's choice. A baseline needs a command that lowers it, or slack accumulates. The source project does not install the kit, so this is a direct contribution rather than an installed-release export.
sanitization: Removed the project's tool, script and task names, host names and paths. The linter and type checker are named only by kind. No credentials, private account data, employer, client or third-party material is included.
